transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… work’s been getting to me more than usual. Since they put me in as acting workflow lead, I’m walking into the warehouse already tense. I’ve been snapping over little SAP mistakes, missing cycle-count deadlines I didn’t used to miss, and by the time I get home I’m just wiped out… not really playing basketball or working on my sketches like I used to.
Are you still enjoying basketball and sketching when you do find the time to do them?
I don’t know… I haven’t really done either enough lately to tell. When I do, it’s kind of hard to get into it, I guess.
Do you feel like you're enjoying things less overall than you used to?
Maybe a little? I’m not really sure. It’s more like I just don’t get around to things, and when I do I’m kind of distracted. I wouldn’t say I’ve totally stopped enjoying everything.
Have you been feeling sad most of the time lately?
Not really most of the time, no. I mean… I get down or frustrated, but I wouldn’t say I’m sad all day or anything.
Do you often feel anxious?
Yeah… I think so. Mostly around work. Since they put me as acting workflow lead, I come in already tense, and little things—like SAP mistakes—set me off more than they should.
Are there things you used to do at work or outside of work that you're avoiding now?

Yeah… I guess so. At work I’ve been putting off some cycle-count stuff, or just not getting it done on time. My supervisor brought it up in a check-in, which was… not great.

Outside of work, I haven’t really been going to basketball, and I don’t make time to sketch like I used to. It’s just like work has kind of taken over.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?
I haven’t really noticed, no. My clothes fit about the same, I think.
Do you have recurring thoughts that you can't stop thinking about?
Not really… I mean, I worry about stuff, but I don’t know if I’d call it recurring thoughts I can’t stop.
Are you avoiding certain tasks or situations because you fear something might go wrong?
I don’t think it’s really that. I mean, I avoid some stuff, but it’s not because I’m picturing something going wrong exactly. It’s more like… I just don’t want to deal with it.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can get stuck worrying a bit, but not like the same thought repeating over and over.
Do you often feel anxious when you're not at work or thinking about work?

Mostly it’s tied to work. Like… if I’m at home and not thinking about the warehouse, I’m usually just tired more than anxious. But it kind of follows me sometimes, especially since they put me as acting workflow lead. I’ll leave there drained and not really feel like playing basketball or working on sketches.
Do you often feel anxious when you're doing things you enjoy, like watching a movie or spending time with friends?

Yeah… kind of. I don’t really get into those things like I used to. I’ve stopped going to basketball, and I don’t really sit down to sketch much anymore. Work just kind of takes over, and then I’m too wound up or drained to enjoy it. My supervisor even brought up some missed cycle-count deadlines, so it’s… it’s starting to show.
Do you often feel anxious when you're not thinking about work or anything related to your job?

Not really, no. If I’m not thinking about the warehouse or the acting lead stuff, the anxiety isn’t usually just sitting there on its own. It’s mostly when work gets in my head… walking in already tense, worrying about SAP mistakes, deadlines I’m missing now. Then I get home and I’m just wiped out.
Do you often feel anxious when you're relaxing or doing nothing?

Not usually, if I’m really just relaxing. It’s more… since they made me acting workflow lead, I walk into the warehouse already tense, and that stuff follows me home. Then I’m too drained to play basketball or sketch.
Is your anxiety mostly about the work situation itself or is it more about the possibility of failing in your new role as acting workflow lead?

It’s mostly the work situation… I think. Since they put me in that acting lead role, I walk in already tense. I do worry about messing it up, like with SAP errors or missing cycle-count stuff, but it’s all tied to that role and the warehouse. Then I get home and I’m just too drained to do much.
How long have you been feeling anxious about work?
About four months, I guess. It started when they merged the inventory teams and put me in that acting workflow lead spot.
Has your anxiety about work been causing problems in your relationships or daily life outside of work?

Yeah… a bit. My supervisor brought up that I’d missed some cycle-count deadlines in a check-in, which was embarrassing. And outside work, I’ve kind of stopped going to basketball and I don’t really sketch like I used to. It feels like work just takes up everything.
Have you noticed any problems in your personal relationships, like with family or friends, since you started feeling anxious about work?
Not really… I mean, I’ve been more quiet, maybe harder to get ahold of, but I haven’t noticed any big problems with family or friends. I mostly just keep to myself when I’m worn out.
Are you finding it harder to do everyday tasks outside of work because of your anxiety?

Yeah… mostly stuff I used to do after work. I’ve stopped making it to basketball, and I don’t really sit down to sketch anymore. It’s like work spills over and I just don’t have the headspace. And, I mean, my supervisor already had to bring up some missed cycle-count deadlines, so it’s affecting things.
Have you felt like you're unable to cope with the stress of your new role at work?

Yeah… I guess so. Since they made me acting workflow lead, I feel tense before I even get into the warehouse. Little SAP mistakes get under my skin, and I’ve missed cycle-count deadlines I normally wouldn’t. Then I go home wiped out and don’t really do basketball or sketching anymore. So… yeah, it feels like I’m not handling it that well.
